stem: Which statement about the size of a skin prick test wheal is correct?

options.text: It indicates the likelihood of allergy but not the severity of a reaction
It guarantees anaphylaxis if it is larger than 10 mm
It is only relevant in children older than 2 years
It must be measured exactly 60 minutes after the prick
It rules out allergy if it is small

explanation: It indicates the likelihood of allergy but not the severity of a reaction. A larger wheal makes true sensitisation more likely, but it does not predict whether any reaction will be mild or severe.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a larger wheal increases the likelihood of clinical allergy, but wheal size does not predict reaction severity.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a large wheal does not guarantee anaphylaxis or any specific reaction severity.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because wheal size interpretation is relevant across paediatric ages, although cut-offs and interpretation may vary.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because skin prick tests are usually read after about 15 to 20 minutes, not 60 minutes.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a small wheal does not exclude allergy, especially when history suggests sensitisation.

source.hint: Recall the distinction between the probability of reacting and the intensity of that reaction.
